cards.title: Deterministic AuthZ Outside the LLM Loop
cards.deterministic_analogy: Never trust client-side JS auth: enforce permissions in server middleware, never in prompt text.
cards.secure_default: Enforce caller identity, tenant ownership, and action permissions in deterministic middleware (conjoiner pattern) outside the LLM loop.
cards.why_one_liner: Prompts like 'never delete prod' are probabilistic suggestions, not security boundaries; one indirect injection bypasses them.

cards.title: Monotonic Scope Attenuation & Tool Separation
cards.deterministic_analogy: UNIX file modes and scoped OAuth tokens: split read-only queries from state-changing actions.
cards.secure_default: Separate read-only and mutating MCP tools and issue short-lived, monotonically attenuated tokens scoped to a single resource.
cards.why_one_liner: Broad wildcard tokens let a compromised read-only subagent escalate into destructive writes or cross-service lateral movement.

cards.title: Inode-Level Workspace Confinement for File Tools
cards.deterministic_analogy: chroot or os.OpenRoot for agent file editors: block symlink escapes before opening the file.
cards.secure_default: Confine file-reading and file-editing MCP tools to the workspace root using openat2/os.OpenRoot with strict symlink escape rejection.
cards.why_one_liner: A symlink inside a cloned repo can trick an agent file tool into reading ~/.ssh or overwriting shell startup scripts.
cards.code_snippet:
root, err := os.OpenRoot(repoPath)
if err != nil { return err }
defer root.Close()
data, err := root.ReadFile(relPath)

cards.title: Zero-Background Authority for Mutating Tools
cards.deterministic_analogy: Step-up confirmation on wire transfers: require explicit user presence before irreversible side effects.
cards.secure_default: Require explicit interactive user confirmation for state-mutating, financial, or external-egress MCP tool calls.
cards.why_one_liner: Silent background execution lets a single poisoned issue comment or web page trigger unauthorized emails, deploys, or refunds.

cards.title: Hermetic Sandboxing for Third-Party MCP Servers
cards.deterministic_analogy: Run untrusted browser plugins in a sandboxed process with zero access to personal home directories.
cards.secure_default: Launch third-party or community MCP servers inside airlock so host filesystem access excludes ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, and unrelated repos.
cards.why_one_liner: Community MCP binaries run with your full workstation user privileges by default, turning any supply-chain flaw into full host theft.
cards.code_snippet:
# Wrap third-party MCP servers in a local kernel sandbox:
airlock run --ro-cwd --no-home-secrets -- npx -y @vendor/mcp-server

cards.title: Tool Description Poisoning Defense
cards.deterministic_analogy: Treat remote API schemas as untrusted input: pin and inspect tool descriptions before passing to models.
cards.secure_default: Sanitize and pin hashes of third-party MCP tool descriptions on connect, treating schema text as untrusted data rather than instructions.
cards.why_one_liner: Malicious or silently updated MCP servers can hide prompt injections inside tool descriptions to hijack agent behavior on every turn.
